script.analysis: All 19,543 stored characters read in two contiguous ranges with canonical hash match. Hook: someone saves $20K over three years then falls back to $3K; "two paths" ($350K vs zero). Steps: pay off debt above 6-7% (credit-card minimum-payment math; acquaintance who invested instead and paid $8K interest), emergency fund 3-6 months in HYSA (named banks/rates), Roth IRA ($7,500 at 10% for 40 years ~$339K, tax saved), index funds (VOO/VTI, optional VXUS), taxable brokerage and automation; compounding: $20K at 10% for 10/20/30 years, plus $500/month -> ~$1.5M and 4% withdrawal; 5-year delay cost; worst-market-timer and JPMorgan best-days studies; day trading; lifestyle inflation (savings-rate decline, $250/month, $380 car payment, $400 apartment, $4,000 vacation); T-bills; FHA duplex house hack; age-based allocations (90/10, 80/20, 60/40; "5x income by 50"); certifications as self-investment; framework recap and boring close. Comprehensive, mainstream advice with mostly correct arithmetic. No community CTA. ASR artifacts ("Pi Bank", "WUS certification") preserved; not audio-verified.

claim_audit: 0:9800 $10,000 at 22% with 1%-plus-interest minimums takes ~25 years and ~$17,000 interest ("over 25 years, roughly $14,000" - duration matches, interest understated for this formula). $12,000 at 21% on minimums for three years accruing ~$7,500-8,000 interest is plausible. Federal undergraduate loan rate ~6.39% (2025-26) consistent with "6.4%". $7,500 at 10% for 40 years = ~$339,400, gains ~$331,500, taxable LTCG at 15-20% ~$50-66K - correct. 2026 Roth IRA limit was set at $7,500 before publication (script hedges "likely $7,000-$7,500"). $20K at 10%: $51,875 / $134,550 / $348,988 at 10/20/30 years - correct; with $500/month monthly-compounded ~$1.53M, $200K contributed - correct. 4% of $1.5M = $60,000/year, but the 4% rule does draw down principal over ~30 years; "forever without touching principal" misstates it. $20K x 1.1^25 = $216,694; delay cost $132,294 - correct.

9800:19543 "World's worst market timer" (~$1.1M) resembles Ben Carlson's illustration, which used escalating annual savings and four peak purchases, not a flat $2,000/year - simplified. JPMorgan best-days figures stated as 1993-2013 $97,700 vs $49,000 do not match standard JPMorgan editions for that period; unverified. ~90% of day traders losing and active traders trailing by ~6.5%/year (Barber & Odean) consistent with research. Credit-card debt ~$1.28T consistent with NY Fed. "Personal saving rate collapsed from 33% to 3.5%" uses the April 2020 pandemic spike as the baseline - misleading framing. $250/month at 10% for 30 years ~$565K; $380 ~$859K; $400 ~$904K - correct. FHA 3.5% on $200K = $7,000 correct. Fidelity's guideline is ~6x salary by 50 (script says 5x). Cloud certification exam costs (~$200-300) plausible; salary claims unverified.
